final_answer:
Let  
\[
m=2q^2,\qquad G=\mathbb F_3^2.
\]
Then \(\pi\) is a fixed-point-free involution on \([n]\), written as the product of the \(m\) transpositions
\[
T_r=\{r,\bar r\}\qquad (1\le r\le m).
\]

Because the only cube-relations among
\[
p_1,p_2,g_1,\dots,g_n,h_1,\dots,h_n
\]
are the two global ones \(\prod_i g_i\in (M^\times)^3,\ \prod_i h_i\in (M^\times)^3\), Kummer theory gives that every \(\sigma\in\Gal(L/\mathbf Q(\omega))\) with \(\pi_\sigma=\pi\) has a unique description
\[
\sigma(\alpha_i)=\omega^{a_i}\alpha_{\pi(i)},\qquad
\sigma(\beta_i)=\omega^{b_i}\beta_{\pi(i)},\qquad
\sigma(\rho_1)=\omega^c\rho_1,\qquad
\sigma(\rho_2)=\omega^d\rho_2,
\]
with \(a_i,b_i,c,d\in\mathbb F_3\), \(\sum_i a_i=\sum_i b_i=0\).  
The conditions \(\sigma(\rho_1)\neq\rho_1,\ \sigma(\rho_2)\neq\rho_2\) mean
\[
c,d\in\mathbb F_3^\times.
\]

For each transposition-block \(T_r=\{r,\bar r\}\), set
\[
A_r=a_r+a_{\bar r},\qquad B_r=b_r+b_{\bar r}\in\mathbb F_3.
\]
Then
\[
\sum_{r=1}^m A_r=\sum_{r=1}^m B_r=0.
\]

For \((k,\ell)\in\mathbb F_3^2\), \(\sigma\) acts on
\[
\left(\omega^u\rho_1^k\frac{\alpha_i}{\alpha_j},\ \omega^v\rho_2^\ell\frac{\beta_i}{\beta_j}\right)
\]
by
\[
(i,j,u,v)\mapsto \bigl(\pi(i),\pi(j),\,u+kc+a_i-a_j,\,v+\ell d+b_i-b_j\bigr).
\]
Since \(\pi\) is an involution with no fixed points, every orbit on ordered pairs \((i,j)\) has size \(2\). If \(i\in T_r,\ j\in T_s\), then \(\sigma^2\) translates \((u,v)\in\mathbb F_3^2\) by
\[
\bigl(2kc+A_r-A_s,\ 2\ell d+B_r-B_s\bigr).
\]
Hence that 2-point orbit contributes:

- \(9\) cycles of length \(2\) iff
  \[
  A_r-A_s=kc,\qquad B_r-B_s=\ell d;
  \]
- otherwise \(3\) cycles of length \(6\).

So the cycle type on \(\Omega_{k,\ell}\) is determined by the number
\[
N_{k,\ell}=\#\{\text{ordered-pair orbits with }A_r-A_s=kc,\ B_r-B_s=\ell d\}.
\]

Now let
\[
z_r=(A_r,B_r)\in G,\qquad
T_g=\#\{r:z_r=g\}\quad(g\in G).
\]
For \(t\in G\), define
\[
C_t=\#\{(r,s):r\neq s,\ z_r-z_s=t\}.
\]
Then:

- for \(t\neq 0\), \(N_{k,\ell}=2C_t\) with \(t=(kc,\ell d)\);
- for \((k,\ell)=(0,0)\), there are also the \(m\) same-block orbits, so
  \[
  N_{0,0}=m+2C_0.
  \]

Thus the nine \(\Omega_{k,\ell}\) have the same cycle type iff
\[
m+2C_0=2C_t\qquad(t\neq0),
\]
i.e.
\[
C_t=C_0+q^2\qquad(t\neq0).
\]

Now take the Fourier transform on \(G\). If
\[
S_\chi=\sum_{g\in G}T_g\chi(g),
\]
then the difference-count condition above gives
\[
|S_\chi|^2=q^2\qquad(\chi\neq1),\qquad S_1=\sum_gT_g=m=2q^2.
\]
Set \(L=L_q=(2q^2-q)/9\) and \(Y_g=T_g-L\). Then
\[
\sum_g Y_g=q,
\]
and every Fourier coefficient of \(Y\) has absolute value \(q\).

Since \(q\equiv2\pmod3\), \(q\) is prime in \(\mathbf Z[\omega]\). Therefore each nontrivial Fourier coefficient equals \(q\) times a unit. Inverting the transform shows that each
\[
9Y_g/q
\]
is an integer and also a sum of \(9\) complex numbers of modulus \(1\), one of which is \(1\). Hence it can only be \(0\) or \(9\). Summing over \(g\in G\) gives total \(9\), so exactly one \(g_0\in G\) has
\[
Y_{g_0}=q,
\]
and all other \(Y_g=0\). Therefore
\[
T_{g_0}=L_q+q=H_q,\qquad T_g=L_q\ \ (g\neq g_0).
\]
Because \(\sum_r z_r=0\), the distinguished class must be \(g_0=0\). So necessarily and sufficiently
\[
T_{(0,0)}=H_q,\qquad T_g=L_q\ \ (g\neq0).
\]

This distribution indeed works, because then
\[
C_0=H_q(H_q-1)+8L_q(L_q-1),
\]
and for every \(t\neq0\),
\[
C_t=2H_qL_q+7L_q^2=C_0+q^2.
\]

So we now count such \(\sigma\).

There are

- \(\displaystyle \binom{2q^2}{H_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q}\) ways to assign the \(m=2q^2\) transposition-blocks to the \(9\) values of \(G\), with \((0,0)\) used \(H_q\) times and each nonzero value used \(L_q\) times;
- for each block, \(3\) choices of \((a_r,a_{\bar r})\) with prescribed sum \(A_r\), and independently \(3\) choices of \((b_r,b_{\bar r})\) with prescribed sum \(B_r\), giving
  \[
  3^m\cdot 3^m=3^n
  \]
  total choices;
- \(2\) choices for \(c\in\mathbb F_3^\times\) and \(2\) for \(d\in\mathbb F_3^\times\).

Therefore the number of desired \(\sigma\) is
\[
\boxed{4\cdot 3^n\binom{2q^2}{H_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q}}.
\]

Final answer:
\[
\boxed{4\cdot 3^n\binom{2q^2}{H_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q,L_q}}.
\]
